html:
A Semitic-speaking people of ancient Syria who moved into Mesopotamia around 2100 to 1800 BCE and founded many of its ruling houses. Sumerian texts called them MAR.TU, "westerners", and pictured them as tent-dwelling herders of the Syrian steppe.

The kings of Ur III built a long wall to keep them out, but it did not hold. After Ur fell around 2004 BCE, Amorite chiefs took power in city after city: Isin, Larsa, Mari and Babylon. Shamshi-Adad I built a large kingdom in the north that took in Assyria, and Hammurabi of Babylon, also of Amorite descent, united the south into the Old Babylonian kingdom. In Syria the Amorite kingdom of Yamhad ruled from Aleppo.

They kept their own names and gods but adopted Akkadian speech and cuneiform writing, and blended into the older population. By about 1600 BCE they no longer appear as a distinct people, though the Hebrew Bible still names the Amorites among the peoples of Canaan.
